segments.text: More than 26 years prior to the main story, a woman calling herself Shino had left her hometown in the countryside where she had no family or work to support her, and somehow made it to Tokyo while earning a meager daily wage. She was haggard and on the verge of starvation when she met Fumichika Nejima, who had tried to perform a black magic ritual to summon a partner for himself. Fumichika, who felt a connection with Shino due to the ritual, decided to take her into his home and let her live there. Both of them having lived alone for most of their lives, the two turned out to be a perfect match.

Shino gradually recovered, but still was not strong enough to work. Fumichika was by no means a skilled businessman, and their lives were far from financially secure, but Shino, who had experienced wartime Japan, was simply content to have food on the table to eat every day. The two spent their days together, poor but happy to be by each other's sides.

Several years later, Shino's condition to a severe turn for the worse. The local doctor could offer them no help and, without enough money to take Shino to a major hospital, Fumichika resorted to using black magic to heal her. However, it was no use, and she passed away at their home. Her final words were: I'm sorry I must go first. I'll leave the rest to you."
Edited from in-game Persons of Interest profile for Nejima

Dahlia asked Iris to live her life at Ivy University in the event of another encounter with law enforcement, and to retake the bottle from Wright.

Six months went by and the bottle necklace was not recovered. Having failed in the task for all that time, Dahlia suspected that Iris had actually fallen in love with Wright. Without Iris’ knowledge, Dahlia took matters into her own hands and went back to the university herself in desperation. She attempted to kill Wright by stealing more of Swallow's poison and using it to poison Wright's cold medicine. However, before her plan could come to fruition, she found Swallow trying to warn Wright about her and the stolen poison. Dahlia then permanently silenced Swallow by using power cables to fatally electrocute him, and attempted to frame Wright for his murder. Mia had finally decided to return to the courtroom for the first time since Fawles' trial. She took on Wright's case and Dahlia was then convicted and sentenced to death, but swore that she would someday have her revenge against the woman who had defeated her.

One month after her execution, Godot and Misty Fey learned of Morgan's plot and tried to stop it by having Misty channel Dahlia instead. However, this aura of innocence was a façade, and when pressed into a corner, her demeanor could change to a terrifying, almost demonic visage. Furio "The Tiger" Tigre was the owner of loan shop Tender Lender, operating it alongside his assistant, Viola Cadaverini. He testified as a witness in the retrial of Maggey Byrde for the murder of Glen Elg.

One day, Tigre got involved in a hit-and-run on a car while riding his scooter, injuring the car's driver. Unfortunately for him, the driver, Viola, was the granddaughter of powerful mob boss Bruto Cadaverini. Bruto was furious and demanded from Tigre the $1 million required for the surgery to save Viola's life.

Short on time, Tigre called in all the loans he could. One of his debtors was Elg, who had accumulated a particularly large debt from his gambling addiction on top of Tender Lender's interest rate. Viola, meanwhile, became infatuated with Tigre, unaware of the reason he was paying her medical bills. She began assisting him in his business, to his chargin as he disliked her, but he pretended to appreciate it out of fear of further angering Bruto.

On December 3, Elg met Tigre at the French restaurant Trés Bien, intending to repay the loan by giving him the disc containing MC Bomber, a computer virus that would sell for millions of dollars on the black market. Unfortunately for Tigre, during the meeting, Elg, who was listening to the radio with an earpiece, won the grand prize of the city's local lottery. The prize was enough to pay Elg's debts, but not enough to handle Tigre's. Desperate, Tigre killed Elg by poisoning him and took the disc. He then acted out the murder for the purposes of providing a false witness in Victor Kudo and framing Byrde, who worked at the restaurant; Tigre posed as Elg, while Viola posed as Byrde. Restaurant owner Jean Armstrong, who was indebted to Tigre, was forced to help with the charade. However, Tigre was unaware that the recreation contained a number of mistakes, most notably Elg's earpiece being in the wrong ear.

Tigre then proceeded to disguise himself as the famous defense attorney Phoenix Wright, complete with a cardboard attorney's badge, and offered to defend Byrde in court. Byrde was ultimately taken in by the deception and accepted. Tigre lost the trial against prosecutor Winston Payne, resulting in Byrde's conviction. After the trial, Tigre sold MC Bomber, keeping the original CD of the program for himself, and paid the surgery bill. The virus would later be used to attack the servers of the Criminal Affairs Department.

The following month, the real Wright appealed Byrde's case after hearing about it from Dick Gumshoe. After a first encounter with Wright in which Tigre tried to make him pay for allegedly soiling his scooter, the loan shark quickly retreated upon learning of the latter's identity, flippantly declaring that he himself was "Phoenix Wright". Wright later visited Tender Lender's office, where, after finding evidence of Tigre's deception in court, he once again met face-to-face with Tigre, who once again tried to coerce money out of Wright using the excuse of a soiled carpet. However, Viola's admission of guilt for this particular accident made Tigre relent and leave the scene, but not before threatening Wright to cease trying to ruin his plan.

After speaking with Viola, and making her realize Tigre's true role in her incident, Wright obtained her medical papers. In response, Tigre ambushed Wright at Trés Bien, where he once again forced Armstrong to support him. Tigre roughed up Wright, and was about to burn the medical papers with a lighter, if not for Gumshoe's timely intervention, which allowed Wright to flee with the papers while Gumshoe held off Tigre.

The next day, Wright was able to force Armstrong to confess about his coercion by Tigre, which made the prosecutor, Godot, ask for a recess in order to subpoena him. Despite Tigre's many attempts to dodge accusations, Wright tricked him into implicating himself by presenting a bottle containing Elg's ear medicine and claiming that it was the poison used to kill him; Tigre laughed and made an outburst that corrected him, explaining, in intricate detail, the type of bottle that held the poison, something he would have been unable to do if he was not the killer. Upon realizing his mistake, Tigre screamed, which caused all the lights in the courtroom to break. Viola later implied that she sent poisoned, or at least in some way tainted, tea to him in prison.

He had his body created by the Girl in the Illusionary World out of garbage so that he can be with her. The body is about half the girl's height. He can't talk as he has been created without a mouth, so he relies on body language to communicate with the girl. He can't feel warmth or cold either.

This is Tomoya himself after his death. His soul traveled across dimensions and entered this fake body in order to be with the girl. He does not remember this but holds vague memories of another lively, warm world, which eventually leads him to convince the girl to leave the Illusionary World to look for a better place. He, however, is not human, and can't create things out of garbage.

His greatest wish is for the girl to be happy. For this purpose, they try to create another robot to keep them company, although they fail, and construct a playground. The girl then tried to create a flying machine, but winter comes and she is forced to stop. The robot tries to help, but can't make anything useful. They then set out together on a journey on foot trying to escape from the Illusionary World. When the girl is on the edge of death, she tells him to collect light orbs to create a miracle to save Nagisa, Ushio and himself from tragedy. Afterward, he and the girl revert to their original selves.

The business of Tenjou Foods, which was run by her father, rapidly deteriorated. Part of the business was transferred to a Tokyo-based company known as “Sakunamite", Her family moved to Tokyo in order to revive the business. However, Tenjou Foods went bankrupt with only the food distribution division being taken over.

The dream of reviving the business completely disappears. Rina's father becomes ill, due to continued heartache and the shattering of his dreams. Rina is admitted into college, but life is hard having to work, take care of her father, and study.

Then, Yasuhito Sakurada, one of the grandsons of the chairman of “Sakunamite,” takes a shine to her and asks her to marry him. At first, Rina refused, but Yasuhito offered financial support, suggesting that she could stay at home as a full-time housewife without having to work part-time and could instead take care of her father.
Completely exhausted both physically and mentally, and considering her father's worsening health, Rina accepted Yasuhito’s marriage proposal and became his wife.

They leave their shabby apartment and are welcomed into Yasuhito's home as his wife, and begin to live together as husband and wife. However, within three months of their union, she discovered that Yasuhito had several mistresses. When asked about it, Yasuhito responded that he could do whatever he wanted with his money. Rina began regretting how easily she agreed to the marriage. Although dissatisfied, she continued caring for her father.

Yasuhito's behaviour continued to get worse by the day, and would not return home for days at a time. To add insult to injury, her father is diagnosed with liver cancer. All sorts of medication and surgeries were tried, but it had already metastasized and was too late for him. 6 months after diagnosis, he had passed away.

With Rina's father now gone, she feels suffocated living with Yasuhito and leaves home to live separately. The relationship has fully deteriorated. Rina returns to her shabby apartment, but Yasuhito does not agree to divorce, rather he wants to keep her as part of his mistress collection. Rina is unsettled by this, not knowing what his intentions are.

Rina thought that she needs to continue living for her parents who had passed away unexpectedly, and that running away from the painful reality would not solve anything. She is determined to make a new life for herself. Rina reunites with Nachi who had been searching for her, and the two begin a new life with each other.
